Calculate Bootstrap Prediction Intervals

Source: R/gam_fitting.R
boot2ci_PI.Rd

Prediction intervals from bootstrap refits of the monotone GAM, using the out-of-bag predictions as out-of-sample residuals.

Usage

boot2ci_PI(loess_boot, fit, newdata, alpha = 0.05)

Arguments

loess_boot

A boot object from boot::boot() with gam_mono_con_fun(), run with newdata = c(newdata, rt_source), i.e. predicting at the grid followed by the calibration compounds. It must not be pruned yet.

fit

Output of fit_gam_mono() on the full data.

newdata

Numeric vector of x-values for the prediction grid.

alpha

Significance level for PI (default 0.05 for 95% PI).

Value

A matrix with 3 columns: [predicted, lower, upper] at each newdata point.

Details

Each compound is predicted by the refits whose resample did not contain it (out-of-bag, on average 37% of the refits). Its residual from the mean out-of-bag prediction is an out-of-sample error that includes the uncertainty of the fitted curve. A compound that is in every resample gets the leave-one-out residual of the unconstrained GAM instead. These residuals then go through the same local scale model and conformal calibration as gam_adaptive_pi() (conformal_band()), around the full-data fit. This is the jackknife+-after-bootstrap idea of Kim, Xu & Barber (2020).

References

Kim, B., Xu, C. & Barber, R. F. (2020). Predictive inference is free with the jackknife+-after-bootstrap. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 33, 4138-4149.
